hardware_answers.question: Do the short source forms esp32c5-ttyACMn, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACMn and esp32c5btle-ttyACMn work on real boards with the current C helper (and the same names with the Python remote helper)?

answers.answer: Yes for the C helper, local and --connect. esp32c5-ttyACM0, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 and esp32c5btle-ttyACM2, run one at a time, each gave 'capturing (wifi|zigbee|btle)' 1.50 s after launch. All four together (two Wi-Fi, zigbee, btle) ran with dlt 127/230/256 and hop lists 42 (1..177) / 16 (11-26) / 1 (37). C --connect worked with esp32c5-ttyACM1 and esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2. The Python remote helper worked with esp32c5-ttyACM1, esp32c5btle-ttyACM3 and esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 (the last with channel options). Python zigbee without options was not run separately.
answers.evidence: g1a/g1b/g1c logs ('esp32c5-ttyACM0 capturing (wifi)' 1.988 s, 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 capturing (zigbee)' 1.965 s, 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' 1.972 s). n1c/g4 src.json. n8t, n9 ('esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 - esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2 capturing (zigbee)', 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM3 - /dev/ttyACM3 capturing'), n4r.

answers.answer: This adds to the first agent's run. The BTLE short forms worked on real boards: C local '-c esp32c5btle-ttyACM0' and '-c esp32c5btle-ttyACM2', and '--source esp32c5btle-ttyACM2' through both the C remote and the Python remote helper. So did 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2:channel=20,channel_hop=false' and 'esp32c5-ttyACM2', through all three setups. Log lines: 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM0 capturing (btle)' (local), 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' (C remote), 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - /dev/ttyACM2 capturing' (Python remote).
Yes, the short source forms work with the Python remote helper on real boards: esp32c5-ttyACMn, esp32c5zigbee-ttyACMn and esp32c5btle-ttyACMn, alone or several in one process.
answers.evidence:
All ran with running=1. Link type and hop list per radio:
- esp32c5-ttyACM0: link type 127, 42 channels 1..177.
- esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM2: 230, 16 channels 11..26.
- esp32c5btle-ttyACM3: 256, [37].

Python sources on the log lines appear as '<name> - <port> capturing', not '<name> capturing (wifi)'. The C local and C remote sources for the same boards also captured in p2 (b/c).

The four-source run (p10a) and the mix of C local and Python (p10b) also used these names.

hardware_answers.question: BLE on the air: is BLE 5 extended advertising not captured? Is SCAN_RSP never captured (passive scan), so names sent only in scan responses are missing? What scan duty cycle does the controller really give?

answers.answer: Passive parts settled; the active parts (own adverts from hci0) could not be run. (1) Extended advertising: none is captured. The firmware uses the legacy NimBLE passive scan and drops any report with more than 31 data bytes (sniff_ble: data_len > 31 -> s_oversize++). In 12,695 records from 6 captures, the only PDU types were ADV_IND (0) and ADV_NONCONN_IND (2), and the longest AdvData was 31 bytes (2217 of 3644 records at exactly 31). No extended advertiser nearby was known, so absence on air is shown but not proven against a known source. (2) SCAN_RSP: 0 in 12,695 records (PDU type 4 never seen), and no ADV_SCAN_IND or ADV_DIRECT_IND either. So a device that names itself only in a scan response will appear without a name (inferred, not shown with a known device). The wiki's 'scan responses are rare' is effectively 'never'. (3) Duty cycle: the scan listens almost continuously. The strongest regular advertiser (0e:0a:43:01:2a:dd, -34 dBm, 100 ms interval, median gap 105.0 ms, minimum 98.9 ms) was heard 1119 times in 120 s against 28 missed events: 97.6% of its advertising events. The largest gap in the whole stream was 197 ms. Weaker advertisers were heard less often (61-81%), limited by signal. (4) The Pi's own hci0 cannot be used without sudo: 'PowerState: off-blocked' (rfkill soft block) and /dev/rfkill is root:root 0664. So there was no own advertising at a known interval, no extended-advert test and no active-scan name comparison.
answers.evidence: hw2/results-ble-oldfw/b9raw.json, b9raw.out, b9k.an, f10raw.json; firmware/main/esp32c5_sniffer.c:542-550, 1175-1183; bluetoothctl show; ls -la /dev/rfkill

hardware_answers.question: Does a board on the sibling's 1.2.0 web-flasher image sync and capture Wi-Fi, zigbee and btle under both final helpers? What are the BTLE fix-up behaviour and message text, and the length checks (no false drops)?

answers.answer: Yes, on the Kismet side (the extcap part, id 130, was not run). Board D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image synced and captured all three radios under the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers. Wi-Fi: 792 / 516 / 342 packets. Zigbee: 200/200 TXTEST frames each, link type 230. BTLE: 2536 / 1141 / 633 packets, with 13/12/12 devices. The board sends flags 0x0013 and a zero CRC. Every helper rewrites each record to 0x0C13 with a valid CRC (100% of 4,323 pcapng packets checked) and logs this once per helper connection, verbatim: '<name>: the board's firmware does not mark BTLE packets as CRC checked, so Kismet would drop them; the helper fills in the CRC and the flags (the board only reports packets whose CRC passed). Flashing current firmware makes this unnecessary'. In Kismet it reads 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a local source and 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a remote one. There were 0 'impossible length' drops and 0 error packets. The only differences from current firmware are the fix-up message and the 0x0013 flags on the wire.
answers.evidence: f10w.out, f10z.out, f10b.out, f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10raw.json

answers.answer: Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.

hardware_answers.question: With the sibling's firmware 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, what happens in btle mode (and in zigbee mode on 1.0.0) with both helpers: the 'lost sync (the board sends link type X, not Y)' and 15 s message texts, and the retry cadence? Does Wi-Fi still work?

answers.answer: 1.1.0 (sha256 3453d366...): Wi-Fi 613 packets; Zigbee 200/200. BTLE fails: MODE BLE is silently ignored (no reboot, the stream stays link type 127). The C local helper then logs pairs once every 0.5-1.0 s (34 pairs in 40 s): 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 capturing (btle)' followed by 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)'. At 15.5 s the helper exits and Kismet shows only 'Data source ... encountered an error: IPC connection closed' and 'Kismet will attempt to re-open the source in 5 seconds. (1 failures)'. It re-opens at +5.1 s, a cycle of about 20 s. The helper's own 15 s text never appears (see problems). The Python helper logs '/dev/ttyACM2 capturing' followed by '/dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256)' every 0.9 s. At 15.6 s Kismet shows 'encountered an error: remote connection triggered shutdown: the board on /dev/ttyACM2 has not been capturing for 15 s (last: /dev/ttyACM2: lost sync (the board sends link type 127, not 256))', and it reconnects 5.1 s later. 1.0.0 (sha256 6a9c108f...): zigbee and btle fail the same way ('... not 283' / '... not 256'). The Python zigbee give-up came at 23.1 s in the first cycle, not 15 s. Wi-Fi does NOT work: START is answered with link type 127, but 0 records ever arrive (0 packets in 40 s under Kismet, 0 bytes raw).

Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: The C helper's 15 s give-up message never reaches Kismet: users see only 'IPC connection closed'
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: Seen in 4 of 4 local give-ups (o110.btle.log, o100.btle.log, o100.zigbee.log, earlier n15.log): 0 occurrences of 'no capture from the board', and REST error_reason is 'IPC connection closed'. The helper writes the text as v3 CMD_ERROR (strace in hw2/results/hw2/strace/esp32c5.283245 line 137). Kismet cfe427074's kis_external.cc:1037-1066 dispatch_rx_packet_v3 has no case for KIS_EXTERNAL_V3_CMD_ERROR.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: At capture_esp32c5.c:1383-1388, send the same text as a message before cf_send_error: cf_send_message(caph, errstr, MSGFLAG_ERROR). Kismet logs MESSAGE frames, and the per-source text then appears. Do the same for the cf_send_error at line 925. Until then, change Bluetooth-LE-Capture.md:86, Zigbee-and-Thread-Capture.md:123 and Flashing-the-Firmware.md:335 to say that a local source shows 'IPC connection closed' and is re-opened every ~20 s.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: Kismet silently drops BLE advertisers whose advertising data ends in zero padding
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: Three GREE (50:2C:C6) advertisers were in the pcapng (182, 200 and 3 packets in 180 s), but no device was created and nothing was logged. Their 31-byte AdvData is 02 01 06 | 12 ff 5d00... | then 9 zero bytes. bluetooth_parsers/btle.cc:40-43 reads length 0 and then read_bytes(length()-1), which throws; phy_btle.cc:257 catches it and returns without a device or error count.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Add a limit: 'Kismet cfe427074 cannot parse advertisements whose data ends in zero padding and never lists those advertisers, although their packets are in the pcapng and kismetdb logs.' Optionally report upstream: stop the AD loop at a zero length byte.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: BLE wiki pages understate how frozen BTLE devices are in a BTLE-only Kismet
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: 180 s run: 15 of 16 devices at packets.total 1 (one at 2), first_time == last_time for all 16, and signal left at the first packet's value. The dedupe ring (packetchain.cc:420-426) advances only on unique packets, and a BTLE-only session adds about 17 unique packets in 3 min, so it never wraps.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Say that the count, last-seen time and signal stay at the first packet until the advertisement's bytes change. The ring turns over only as 1024 new unique packets arrive, which in a BTLE-only session can take hours. Replace the 'first few packets' wording and add the 180 s numbers.

hardware_problems_naming_this_page.summary: BTLE channel=38 and set_channel 38 are accepted, but REST then reports channel '38' while the board scans 37/38/39. With channel=38 Kismet also adds 38 to the hop list.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.evidence: p4: 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM3:channel=38' gave channel '37', hop_channels [37,38]. After set_channel {"channel":"38"}: channel '38', hopping 0. The serial writes were only 'MODE BLE' and 'CHANNELS 37...'.
hardware_problems_naming_this_page.suggested_fix: Report 37 back in the CONFIGREPORT for any BTLE channel (as the start channel does), or document it in Bluetooth-LE-Capture and Channel-Control.
